newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas softens in West, firms in East.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas softens in West, firms in East.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices for Friday delivery were softer in the West but stronger in the East on Thursday, market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices fell an average of six cents to the C$1.33-1.34 per gigajoule (GJ) area, as milder temperatures moved into Alberta.
Temperatures in Calgary are forecast to climb to a high of +3 degrees Celsius Friday and then even higher over the weekend, traders said.
Lending support to the market, traders said, were early storage injections and a small outage at an Alberta gas plant, rated at about 100 million cubic feet per day.
In response to the weaker day market, April AECO prices drifted to about C$1.34, while summer prices showed more resiliency around C$1.37-1.395 per GJ.
Also in anticipation of milder weather, Sumas prices tumbled seven cents to the $1.15-1.20 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) area, with most deals reported done at $1.17.
At Niagara, where temperatures are cooler-than-expected, prices gained about four cents to the $2.10-2.15 per mmBtu range.
